sections.html:
Gresham borders Portland on the northwest and anchors the eastern edge of the metro area in Multnomah County. It covers roughly 23 square miles, with hills along the eastern border and a hilly northeast near Troutdale and the Columbia River. Johnson Creek runs west through town, and Fairview and Wood Village are neighbors.

The 2020 Census counted 114,247 residents, making Gresham the fourth largest city in Oregon. There were 41,333 households, and 52.5 percent of homes were owner-occupied, so owner-occupied houses and rentals both change hands steadily. The median age is 36.3. Multnomah County, with 815,428 residents in 2020, is the most populous county in the state.

Gresham recognizes 16 neighborhoods: Central City, Centennial, Gresham Butte, Historic Southeast, Hogan Cedars, Hollybrook, Kelly Creek, North Central, North Gresham, Northeast, Northwest, Pleasant Valley, Powell Valley, Rockwood, Southwest and Wilkes East.

Use the right name in your listing, since the neighborhood tells a buyer a lot before they ever see the house. Buyers often search by area, and trails nearby, including the Springwater Corridor, the 40-Mile Loop and the Gresham-Fairview Trail, are worth a mention. Main City Park sits near downtown.

sections.h2: Which school district is your house in?
sections.html:
Three districts serve Gresham: Centennial, Gresham-Barlow and Reynolds. High schools include Gresham, Sam Barlow, Springwater Trail, Centennial and Reynolds, and Mount Hood Community College is in the city.

Two houses a few blocks apart can feed different schools. Check the district's boundary map for your address and be ready to tell buyers the answer, since it is one of their first questions.

Interstate 84 gives western access and U.S. Route 26 gives eastern access. TriMet buses and the MAX Blue Line light rail serve the city, and the Blue Line's eastern end is at Cleveland Avenue. A fareless Sandy Area Metro shuttle links Gresham to Sandy.

Gresham is at the eastern end of the Portland transit network, so commuters weigh it against houses closer in. Homes near MAX or a major bus line are easier to pitch to buyers without a car.

Gresham has wet winters and dry summers. December is the wettest month at 7.61 inches, annual precipitation is 47.78 inches, and snow adds up to 5.8 inches a year. July and August highs reach 82 degrees on average. Relative humidity averages 75 percent.

That much damp keeps pressure on roofs, gutters, siding and crawl spaces. Houses from the suburban building boom may need new roofs, updated windows or drainage work, and buyers' inspectors will look for all of it.

Gresham allows accessory dwelling units, capped by size. Renting one requires a residential rental license, and short-term rentals, including bed and breakfasts, are prohibited in an ADU. Each unit needs three paved on-site parking spaces, each 8.5 feet by 18 feet.

ADU typeSize limit
Conversion or ADU attached to the houseUp to 900 square feet
Beside or behind a garageUp to 750 square feet, including the garage
Freestanding750 square feet or 50 percent of the house size, whichever is less

Size limits for accessory dwelling units.

Simple conversions go through Type I review in about two to three weeks. Attached additions that enlarge the footprint and most freestanding units go through Type II review, which takes roughly three to four months. An ADU or garage conversion built without permits can complicate a sale, so confirm its status with the city planner before you list.

Multnomah County bills go out by October 25. The three installments fall on November 15, February 15 and May 15, and a lump payment by November 15 takes 3 percent off, while two-thirds takes 2 percent off.

A late installment accrues 1.333 percent a month, counted from December 16, February 16 or May 16. Bills under $40 cannot be split. Measure 50, approved on May 20, 1997, replaced Measure 47. Whatever is still unpaid at closing is deducted from your proceeds, so get the payoff figure from the title company ahead of time.

sections.h2: What a Gresham seller must tell the buyer
sections.html:
Under ORS 105.464, a Gresham seller of covered residential property signs a disclosure statement for every buyer who puts an offer in writing. Topics include title, water, sewage, structure, systems, flooding, settling and other defects. After getting it, the buyer has five days to revoke unless that right was waived.

A personal representative, trustee or conservator selling, and a bank selling after foreclosure, are excluded. Because the form reflects your own knowledge, list the problems you know about and fill in every answer. A garage conversion or added unit done without a permit belongs in that conversation too.

Once you agree on terms, a title company opens escrow and searches the property for liens, unpaid installments and anything that clouds ownership. In Gresham, the usual snags are an unpermitted ADU or garage conversion, a tax installment still open, and heirs who have not yet been cleared to sign.

Clear those items early. Ask the city planner about permit status, request a tax payoff from the title officer, and confirm who has authority to sign for an estate. Then the closing itself is mostly a matter of signing, with the deed recorded and your proceeds released after payoffs.

• Houses from the suburban building boom that need roof, window or drainage updates before a buyer will pay full price.
  • Inherited homes in neighborhoods such as Rockwood or Historic Southeast, where heirs live elsewhere.
  • Landlords with tenants in a house they no longer want to manage.
  • Owners with unpermitted ADUs or garage conversions.
  • Homeowners behind on payments who want certainty on timing.

Selling for cash means no repairs, no showings and no waiting on a lender. You and the title company pick the closing date together. Multnomah County records the deed, and the mortgage and any unpaid tax are paid off from the proceeds.

We buy houses in Gresham in their current condition, and the offer request takes only a few minutes. Before you decide, compare a written cash offer with the cost of repairs, agent fees and months of carrying the house on a regular listing.

Keep your latest tax statement, mortgage payoff figure and any ADU permit records handy. If a tenant lives there, add the lease so the buyer knows what comes with the house, and mention the school district for the address.

faqs.q: How many people live in Gresham?
faqs.a: The 2020 Census counted 114,247 residents, and the estimate for July 1, 2025 is 111,513. Gresham is the fourth largest city in Oregon.

faqs.q: Which district serves my Gresham house?
faqs.a: It depends on the address. Gresham is served by the Centennial, Gresham-Barlow and Reynolds districts, so check the district's boundary map for the exact property.

faqs.q: When is the first Oregon property tax installment due?
faqs.a: November 15. The other two are due February 15 and May 15, and a 3 percent discount applies to full payment by November 15.

faqs.q: Can a Gresham house be sold if it has an unpermitted ADU?
faqs.a: It can be sold, but the buyer may ask about permits, and the city has specific size, parking and review rules for ADUs. Speak with the city's Planner on Duty if the status is unclear.

faqs.q: How big can a Gresham ADU be?
faqs.a: A conversion or attached unit can be up to 900 square feet. A unit beside or behind a garage can be up to 750 square feet including the garage, and a freestanding unit is capped at 750 square feet or 50 percent of the house size, whichever is less.
